A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
refugee children have been found to have a wide range of mental health problems, including depression, anxiety disorders, post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), and conduct disorder.
there is a great need to develop more effective interventions for children who have experienced war and displacement, particularly in low- and middle-income countries.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the mental health consequences of conflict and war are not inevitable and that there is a great deal that can be done to help refugee children.
there is a need for a greater emphasis on prevention and resilience in research and intervention with refugee children.
refugee children are not passive victims of violence, but active agents of their own development.
